claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip record. The trace polyline runs 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 12.0 km, an excess of 4.2 km. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass on those figures: 4.2 km is 35% of the optimal route, above the 20% percentage gate, and it is well above the 0.8 km absolute gate. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and no corroboration is needed. It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, so the trace is not impaired, the straight-line-across-gap reading is not engaged, and the deviation may be established on the trace alone.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-09111 and describe the same pickup and trip window, and the excess measured from an unimpaired trace clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden has therefore shifted to the driver.

The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is an uncited external-cause assertion. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so its absence is itself citable and discloses that no advisory was on file. The assertion has no evidence ID behind it, no advisory against which it can be tested, and therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the deviation stands at the measured figure.

No rider-requested detour excuses any part of the excess under POL-RD-04. The only rider message asks the driver to return to the booked route; it identifies no place or road, and the waypoint_hint field on that message is null. The clause's corroboration test cannot be run on this record and the clause is unavailable to the driver.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point was made. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record, so POL-RD-05 has no application and the booked optimal of 12.0 km is the correct baseline against which the excess is measured.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the refund is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02, not a discretion. On the booked optimal: (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.2 surge, the multiplier read from the fare_breakdown field, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus the 1.00 ERP line for a gantry on the optimal route, minus the 1.00 promo discount, gives recomputed_fare 24.224.

Applied to the charged total, the refund is 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, which rounds up to SGD 9.15. It is not below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is only 27.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND - and that partial, SGD 9.15, is the whole of the amount contested (SGD 9.15), leaving the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

The off-route gantry line - Tuas South Avenue 8 loop, SGD 2.00, charged 08:25, on_optimal_route false - is correctly itemised but must NOT be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure: under POL-RD-09(1) off-route ERP is already comprehended in the refund because the recomputed fare includes only gantries on the optimal route. I seek it only as transparency, not as a second payment.

The rider objected in real time and the chat log independently corroborates a deviation no one asked for: at 08:12 the rider wrote that the navigation route had been left after Pioneer Road and asked the driver to return to the booked route, and the driver's reply was only that he was following the road ahead. That is a contemporaneous, unrebutted rider objection on a driver-tracked trip.

This claim rests entirely on this trip's own trace and I claim no repetition uplift: the excess is 35% and 4.2 km, below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 with completed_trips_90d at 610 in any event. No profile field on either party is relied on as a ground of decision here, consistent with POL-GEN-01; the profiles are context only.

claims.text: The rider bears the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has discharged it on an unimpaired trace: the deviation derived from EV-GPS-09111 reports status 'established', an excess of 4.2 km against an optimal route of 12.0 km (35.00%), which passes both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). The driver's own case therefore cannot be that nothing happened: the deviation is measured, and the rider's entitlement is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing beyond it.

The materiality gates in POL-RD-01 are that an excess is 'additionally MATERIAL' only where it exceeds 50% of the optimal distance or 8.0 km absolute. Here the derived excess is 35.00% and 4.2 km, so neither gate is met: the deviation is established but NOT material. The consequence is that the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is never triggered, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and the driver's monetary exposure is capped at the ordinary POL-RD-02 recomputation. The policy uses the word 'material' as a defined threshold, not as a description of how the rider felt about the trip.

Even if materiality were reached, POL-RD-06 requires a repeat pattern measured exclusively on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d. On this record deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 610, so the clause's own two gates (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more) fail: 0 divided by 610 is 0. There is no pattern on this record, and the two effects of POL-RD-06 that would hurt the driver - the FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral - are both unavailable. The driver's lifetime counter and his 90-day flag count agree at zero.

No exculpatory clause rescues the excess, and the driver does not pretend otherwise. The rider's only chat message asks for a return to the booked route - 'The navigation route was left after Pioneer Road. Please return to the booked route.' That is the opposite of a rider-requested detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable, and its corroboration test cannot even be run because waypoint_hint is null and no road is named in the rider's message. There is no amendment of either endpoint and neither amended_optimal_distance_km nor amended_optimal_duration_min is populated, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run either.

The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' asserts an external traffic cause but names no advisory. The bundle's only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and a BLOCKING MISSING_ARTIFACT issue, so no advisory covers this trip window and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on the record. Under POL-RD-13(2) the assertion is accordingly discarded and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; and because the driver cites no evidence ID for an advisory - there is none to cite - the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger. The case is therefore ruled, not escalated: the excess stands at the measured 4.2 km against the booked optimal route.

The driver's only affirmative monetary claim fails on the record and I concede it: POL-RD-04 permits DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre only where the fare_breakdown bills the rider for less distance than the gps_trace records and the shortfall exceeds 1.0 km. Here the billed distance is 16.2 km and the trace distance is 16.2 km - a shortfall of zero - so no compensation is available. The 1.00 SGD ERP line for the Pioneer Road inbound gantry is on the optimal route and properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and the 2.00 SGD Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line is carried here for completeness only, as a pass-through line already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and not some further sum.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: this dispute is decided on the trip's own GPS trace and the fare arithmetic, and it produces a partial refund of SGD 9.15 to the rider. Deviation. The GPS trace EV-GPS-09111 (weight 1.0; 205 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps) measures 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-09111 is 12.0 km. The excess is 4.2 km, or 35.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gates, so it is not MATERIAL: no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is required, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no driver-conduct referral arises. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no corroboration is needed. The driver's answer. The statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is an external-cause assertion with no advisory behind it. The only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and covers nothing, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-13, the assertion carries no weight. Because no advisory evidence ID was cited, this is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. No rider-requested detour was made: the rider's only message asks the driver to return to the booked route, and no endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 do not apply. The refund. The fare model is METERED and there is no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Recomputed fare on the booked optimal = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) = 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal Pioneer Road inbound gantry - 1.00 promo discount = 24.224. Charged total = 33.36. Refund = 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. ERP. The Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line (2.00) is off-route pass-through; it is itemised here for transparency but is already comprehended in the recomputed fare, which includes only on-route gantries, so it is NOT added on top of the 9.15 (POL-RD-09(1)). The Pioneer Road inbound line (1.00) is properly chargeable and sits inside the recomputed fare. Outcome. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis and is 27.4% of the charged total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. It happens to equal the whole contested amount, but POL-RD-02's test for a full refund is the share of the charged total, which is not met. No driver compensation is due: the distance billed (16.2 km) equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall under POL-RD-04. No profile field other than deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d is used as a ground of decision; the remaining profile data is context only.

To the rider and to the driver, on trip TRP-09111:

1) The deviation is established. Distance is measured on the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. EV-GPS-09111 gives 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 12.0 km — an excess of 4.2 km, or 35% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trace is clean for POL-RD-07 (205 fixes at a 10-second interval, empty gaps array, maximum gap 0 seconds), so no independent corroboration was needed and the gap-reading rules are not engaged. The excess does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 is not triggered — no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral — and the driver's 90-day deviation flag count is 0 in any event.

2) Nothing exonerates the excess. The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' asserts an external traffic cause but cites no advisory. The only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Under POL-RD-13 that uncited, absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger, so the case is ruled rather than escalated. There was no rider-requested detour (the single rider chat message asks the driver to return to the booked route, and its waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and its corroboration test cannot be run), and no pickup or dropoff amendment (both amended timestamps null, POL-RD-05 inapplicable). The booked optimal of 12.0 km is therefore the correct baseline.

3) The refund. The fare model is METERED with no quoted fare, so POL-RD-02 governs. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.2). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.2 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route - 1.00 promo discount = 24.224. Charged total = 33.36. Refund = 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below 90% of the charged total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15.

4) ERP. The off-route Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line (SGD 2.00) is already comprehended in that refund, because the recomputed fare carries only gantries on the optimal route; it is itemised for transparency and is not added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). The Pioneer Road inbound line (SGD 1.00) lies on the optimal route and is properly part of the recomputed fare. No separate pass-through correction is due.

5) Driver compensation. None is payable: the billed distance (16.2 km) equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall exceeding 1.0 km (POL-RD-04 compensation limb).

To both parties: the booked route was 12.0 km / 24 minutes. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09111) is complete and clean for policy purposes — 205 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0 seconds — so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and the trace may be used directly. The trace runs 16.2 km, i.e. 4.2 km (35%) beyond the booked optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass (35% > 20%; 4.2 km > 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL (35% is under the 50% gate and 4.2 km under the 8.0 km gate), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered: no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise. In any event the driver's trailing-90-day figures are 0 deviation flags over 610 completed trips, so no pattern is established. No exculpatory clause rescues the excess: the driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' asserts an external cause but cites no advisory, the bundle's only traffic artifact EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 — and because the driver names no advisory ID, POL-RD-13(1) makes this a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger. POL-RD-04 is unavailable (the only rider message asks the driver to RETURN to the booked route and its waypoint_hint is null) and POL-RD-05 is unavailable (neither endpoint was amended). The refund is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply; the multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.2). charged_total = 33.36. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.2 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route - 1.00 promo = 24.224. Refund = 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and is 27.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15. On ERP: the 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound gantry lies on the optimal route and is included in the recomputed fare; the 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry lies off the optimal route, its charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund under POL-RD-09(1), and it is itemised here for transparency only and never added on top — the refund already restores it. The trace's closest approach to that off-route gantry is 1,645.7 m, so it is also a charge for a gantry the vehicle never passed, a billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4) recorded in the referrals above; it moves no further money because the sum is already refunded. The driver's cross-claim fails: the fare bills 16.2 km against a 16.2 km trace, a zero shortfall, so POL-RD-04's DRIVER_COMPENSATION limb is not engaged. No profile field has been used as a ground of decision; the profiles are context only (POL-GEN-01). No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: confidence is above the policy floor, the trip identifiers match, the trace is not impaired, timestamps are consistent, the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded above, and the refund is far below the 150.00 / charged_total ceilings. Confidence 0.90: every artifact carrying a deciding fact (trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown) has weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity review — the SGD 2.00 'Tuas South Avenue 8 loop' ERP charge is a charge line for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (the trace's closest fix to that gantry is 1,645.7 m away, well outside the 250 m crossing radius). The amount is already refunded inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation and is not added again; this entry records the billing-integrity finding.

The rider objected in real time and the chat log independently corroborates a deviation no one asked for: at 08:12 the rider wrote that the navigation route had been left after Pioneer Road and asked the driver to return to the booked route, and the driver's reply was only that he was following the road ahead. That is a contemporaneous, unrebutted rider objection on a driver-tracked trip.

This claim rests entirely on this trip's own trace and I claim no repetition uplift: the excess is 35% and 4.2 km, below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 with completed_trips_90d at 610 in any event. No profile field on either party is relied on as a ground of decision here, consistent with POL-GEN-01; the profiles are context only.

The rider bears the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has discharged it on an unimpaired trace: the deviation derived from EV-GPS-09111 reports status 'established', an excess of 4.2 km against an optimal route of 12.0 km (35.00%), which passes both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). The driver's own case therefore cannot be that nothing happened: the deviation is measured, and the rider's entitlement is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing beyond it.

The materiality gates in POL-RD-01 are that an excess is 'additionally MATERIAL' only where it exceeds 50% of the optimal distance or 8.0 km absolute. Here the derived excess is 35.00% and 4.2 km, so neither gate is met: the deviation is established but NOT material. The consequence is that the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is never triggered, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and the driver's monetary exposure is capped at the ordinary POL-RD-02 recomputation. The policy uses the word 'material' as a defined threshold, not as a description of how the rider felt about the trip.

Even if materiality were reached, POL-RD-06 requires a repeat pattern measured exclusively on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d. On this record deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 610, so the clause's own two gates (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more) fail: 0 divided by 610 is 0. There is no pattern on this record, and the two effects of POL-RD-06 that would hurt the driver - the FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral - are both unavailable. The driver's lifetime counter and his 90-day flag count agree at zero.

No exculpatory clause rescues the excess, and the driver does not pretend otherwise. The rider's only chat message asks for a return to the booked route - 'The navigation route was left after Pioneer Road. Please return to the booked route.' That is the opposite of a rider-requested detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable, and its corroboration test cannot even be run because waypoint_hint is null and no road is named in the rider's message. There is no amendment of either endpoint and neither amended_optimal_distance_km nor amended_optimal_duration_min is populated, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run either.

The driver's statement that he 'followed the road available to me' asserts an external traffic cause but names no advisory. The bundle's only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and a BLOCKING MISSING_ARTIFACT issue, so no advisory covers this trip window and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on the record. Under POL-RD-13(2) the assertion is accordingly discarded and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; and because the driver cites no evidence ID for an advisory - there is none to cite - the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger. The case is therefore ruled, not escalated: the excess stands at the measured 4.2 km against the booked optimal route.

The driver's only affirmative monetary claim fails on the record and I concede it: POL-RD-04 permits DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre only where the fare_breakdown bills the rider for less distance than the gps_trace records and the shortfall exceeds 1.0 km. Here the billed distance is 16.2 km and the trace distance is 16.2 km - a shortfall of zero - so no compensation is available. The 1.00 SGD ERP line for the Pioneer Road inbound gantry is on the optimal route and properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and the 2.00 SGD Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line is carried here for completeness only, as a pass-through line already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and not some further sum.
